line: Crowley on the Knights: the letter Yodh of the Name, the series Father, Mother, Son, Daughter, and the Father as Knight (pdf p24, p79, p139, p141, p261).

sections.title: The letter of the Name
sections.line: Crowley on the Knights as the powers of the letter Yodh in the Name, and on the Court cards as a pictorial analysis of the four letters and the four Elements (pdf p139).

quotes.quote: The Knights represent the powers of the letter Yodh in the Name.
These cards constitute a pictorial analysis of the powers of the four letters of the Name and the four Elements.

sections.title: Father, Mother, Son, Daughter
sections.line: Crowley on the terms Knight, Queen, Prince and Princess for the series Father, Mother, Son, Daughter (pdf p24), on the Hebrew system (pdf p24), and on the Court cards referred to the numbers 2, 3, 6 and 10 (pdf p261).

quotes.quote: It has been thought better, for the present pack, to adopt the term “Knight”, “Queen”, “Prince” and “Princess”, to represent the series Father, Mother, Son, Daughter, because the doctrine involved, which is extraordinarily complex and difficult, demands it.
The Hebrew system is straightforward and irreversible; it postulates Father and Mother from whose union issue Son and Daughter.
The Court cards are referred to the numbers 2, 3, 6 and 10

sections.title: The Knight as Father
sections.line: Crowley on the Father as Knight, riding on a horse (pdf p24), on Yod as the Father who is Wisdom (pdf p79), and on the moral qualities of the Knight of Wands (pdf p141).

quotes.quote: The Father is “Knight” because he is represented as riding on a horse.
The letter Yod is the first letter of the name Tetragrammaton, and this symbolizes the Father, who is Wisdom;
The moral qualities appropriate to this figure are activity, generosity, fierceness, impetuosity, pride
